summary: Centralize temporary vendor seat pool and implement expense/project tagging for procurement workflow
description:
Issue summary:
We need a standardized approach to provision, track, and reconcile temporary vendor/contractor SaaS seats (30-90 day trials and short-term seats). Current ad-hoc purchases cause billing fragmentation, missing chargeback tags, and repeated manual SCIM/Okta mapping work.

Background and impact:
- Multiple teams request short-term vendor seats (design contractors, security auditors, vendor evaluations). Finance reports cost-center tags are often missing resulting in delayed chargebacks.
- Identity team spends time creating one-off Okta groups and manual SCIM provisioning for each vendor.
- Procurement wants a predictable catalog entry that product teams can select without raising a full PO for small seat requests.
- Without centralization we risk duplicate seat purchases, license overages, and audit gaps.

Request / Objectives:
1) Create a centralized "Temporary Vendor Seat Pool" SKU in the procurement catalog for common SaaS vendors (Notion, Figma, Sentry, PostHog, Snowflake evals).
2) Implement enforced expense/project tagging at provisioning time so Finance receives cost-center and project codes on invoices.
3) Automate onboarding via SCIM/Okta groups with a TTL (default 30 days, extendable) and self-serve UI in the internal procurement portal.
4) Provide an audit report (monthly) listing active temporary seats, owner, project tag, invoice charges, and upcoming expirations.
5) Add Terraform module and a short runbook for infra/identity to adopt for new vendors.

Acceptance criteria:
- Procurement catalog has a "Temp Seat Pool" SKU with SKU code TEMP-SEAT-001 and clear cost thresholds.
- Okta/SCIM automation provisions seats to a tenant group and attaches cost-center/project metadata to the user or group.
- Finance receives invoices with tag metadata or a linked CSV mapping within 72 hours of charge.
- Audit report generated automatically and sent to procurement@redwood.com and cloud-finance@redwood.com on the 1st of each month.
- Runbook and Terraform module merged into internal-repo (link below) with an example for Notion.

Steps already taken / notes:
- Procurement ran a small pilot with Design for two Notion/Abstract trials; learned that vendors differ in SCIM support and invoice metadata.
- Identity scoped Okta group automation; prototype TTL uses a scheduled job that removes users and notifies owner 7 days prior to expiry.
- Finance confirmed they can accept invoice metadata or a reconciled CSV; prefer invoice metadata when available.

Risks / open questions:
- Some vendors (older SaaS) do not populate invoice metadata; we may need to store a reconciled ledger on our side.
- How will seat counts be enforced across Dedicated/Private procurement for contractual enterprise accounts?
- Is there a maximum per-team allocation to avoid misuse?

Attachments / Links:
- Procurement pilot notes: https://confluence.internal.redwood.com/display/PROC/Temp+Seat+Pilot
- Okta automation prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4212
- Terraform module draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/88

Next steps / owner actions:
- Miguel: finalize Terraform module and add Okta TTL job to infra repo (ETA 2026-03-20).
- Asha: update procurement catalog entry and communicate to engineering leads (ETA 2026-03-18).
- Finance (Priya): confirm invoice metadata fields and map to cost-center codes (ETA 2026-03-17).

Notes about timeline: goal is 60-day pilot with Design and Security, then scale to 5 additional teams if metrics (time-to-provision, tagging accuracy, reduction in manual reconciliations) improve by 50%.
